verdict.reasoning: Patient reports onset 2–3 days ago with shortness of breath, wheeze, and cough: "about two to three days ago, I was running with a friend... I found myself actually short of breath" and later "I'm just wheezing a bit, and coughing and just generally a bit short of breath." This is on exertion (running, brisk walking).
Patient describes SOB now with brisk walking: "I'm not really sure of that when I'm walking. Um, but definitely um, if I'm walking briskly now."

She uses the blue (salbutamol) inhaler daily and as needed: Patient says "I've used my blue inhaler but to no avail" and "I think I'm just using that as and when I have symptoms"; when asked if using it every day: "Um, yeah, and morning or evening to kinda prevent it as well."
Normal peak flow discussed as ~380: Doctor says "So, what was what's your peak flow reading when you're good?... Let's see it's about, um, three eighty, yeah?" Patient agrees: "Yeah."

Last asthma attack 3–4 years ago, no admissions, no oral steroids: Doctor asks, "When was the last time you had an asthma attack?" Patient: "about three to four years ago." Doctor asks about hospital admission: "have you ever been admitted in hospital because your was so bad?" Patient: "no, I haven't." Doctor: "have you ever had oral steroids in the past?" Patient: "no."
Asthma review about 2 years ago: Doctor asks, "When was the last time you had an asthma review with our nurse?" Patient: "about two years ago." Doctor repeats, "OK. Two years ago."

History of asthma is implicit from repeated asthma discussion; hay fever is stated: "I have hay fever." Possible eczema is acknowledged: Doctor, "So you'd have eczema also, yeah?" Patient: "I've got a few issues, um, that I think could be eczema as well."
Use of blue salbutamol inhaler: Patient mentions "I've used my blue inhaler" and earlier lists "I'm Salbutamol" among medications. Doctor later says "your salbutamol inhalers."
Preventer inhaler twice daily: Doctor asks "So, how are you using the ? Is it twice a day?" Patient: "Um, yes." This refers to her preventer inhaler.
Cetraben use: After clarification, patient states her meds: "Er, Cetraben and Hydrocortisone."
Hydrocortisone topical: Patient lists "Cetraben and Hydrocortisone," which in context of eczema treatment indicates topical use; doctor links this to eczema: "So you'd have eczema also, yeah?"
No known drug allergies: Doctor asks, "Now any allergies to medication?" Patient: "Ohh no" and doctor concludes, "So you're not allergic to anything?" and notes "So no allergies."
Family history: "my brother is asthmatic" clearly supports brother having asthma.
Family history: Patient states, "my sister has eczema."

Acute exacerbation with 2–3 days SOB, wheeze, cough and poor SABA response: Duration and symptoms stated as above; patient says blue inhaler "hasn't really helped me." Doctor summarizes, "it looks like you can be having a small, small exacerbation."

Increase Clenil to 4 puffs BID: Doctor says, "the brown your Clenil... If you're using just three puffs twice a day, you can increase it to four puffs twice a day" and later repeats, "increase your brown inhaler to four puffs twice a day."

Use SABA PRN up to every 2–4 hours and attend A&E if frequent/ worsening: Doctor: "You can use your blue inhaler as and when... maximum about every two to four, four hours" and later, "your salbutamol inhalers up to every two hourly. But, if you breathing's getting worse and you've not seen us, do take your puffs to A and E."

Urgent GP F2F in next few days for chest exam and PEF: Doctor says, "I would like you to be seen by one of our GP's in the next few days" and later, "I will recommend that meet her face to face." Also, "we're gonna examine your chest... Make you do the peak flow reading."
Consider oral steroids and possibly antibiotics at review depending on findings: Doctor explains, "depending on what we find, you might need some antibiotics and some steroids."
